stem: If $X=\{ {=x0}, {=x1}, {=x2}, {=x3} \}$, $Y=\{ {=y0}, {=y1}, {=y2}, {=y3}, {=y4} \}$, and R is a relation from X to Y where a R b means: «b = {=m}a + {=c}», for each $a\in X$, $b\in Y$. Write R as a set of ordered pairs. Only pairs whose second element belongs to Y are in R. List the pairs in order of a, as (a, b), (a, b), …
solution: When a = {=x0}: b = {=m} × ({=x0}) + {=c} = {=i0}, which is in Y, so ({=x0}, {=i0}) is in R.
When a = {=x1}: b = {=m} × ({=x1}) + {=c} = {=i1}, which is in Y, so ({=x1}, {=i1}) is in R.
When a = {=x2}: b = {=m} × ({=x2}) + {=c} = {=j2}, which is not in Y, so a = {=x2} is in no pair.
When a = {=x3}: b = {=m} × ({=x3}) + {=c} = {=i3}, which is in Y, so ({=x3}, {=i3}) is in R.
constraints: (i2 not in [y0, y1, y2, y3, y4])
notes: Advanced twist like the book's think-and-discuss: one element of X has no partner in Y, so it appears in no pair. Y is built from three true images plus i2+1 and i3+2, neither of which can equal i2 (m>=2). Constraint checks i2 not in Y.
